credit_headline.narrative: Bank credit reached ₹220.8L Cr in July 2026, the highest on record, growing 19.3% year-on-year — the fastest rate in this eleven-period window. psl.narrative: PSL lending is rebalancing from retail-linked categories to productive sectors. Social Infrastructure decelerated sharply by 21.0 points to 36.8%, and Housing slowed 10.7 points to 10.6%, cooling the prior period's retail surge. Renewable Energy surged 11.5 points to 31.7% — the biggest gain in this scan and the fourth consecutive period of acceleration — and is now the second-fastest PSL segment. Medium Enterprises held at 29.2%, Micro and Small Enterprises at 24.1%, and Agriculture at 19.4%, all steady in the mid-teens to high twenties. Weaker Sections held near its series high at 15.2%. Export Credit improved to -8.8% from -10.7%, moderating its decline. The distribution is compressing: the spread narrowed from 68.5pp to 45.6pp as the top cooled and the bottom improved, with 6 of 10 segments now in active status.

chain: Renewable Energy accelerated by 11.54 points, the largest gain in the distribution, while Housing decelerated by 10.66 points and Social Infrastructure by 21.03 points.
The 32.57-point spread between top and bottom is the widest divergence in this dataset, with 4 segments strengthening and 3 weakening.

Export Credit reversed from weakening to strengthening, while Educational Loans broke its stable run and turned weakening — the mix is rotating toward smaller, high-growth segments and away from the prior volume leaders.
sibc-psl-acceleration.inference: PSL growth is fragmenting. Renewable Energy is pulling away at the top while Housing — which drove the prior six months — has decelerated sharply. The 32.57-point spread and four status shifts in one period mark the most volatile rotation in this dataset.
